spots.name: Spodek
spots.summary: Spodek is a multipurpose arena complex in Katowice, Poland, opened on 9 May 1971. Aside from the main dome, the complex includes a gym, an ice rink, a hotel and three large car parks. It was the largest indoor venue of its kind in Poland until it was surpassed by Tauron Arena in 2014.

spots.name: KTW
spots.summary: KTW is a complex of two high-rise buildings in Katowice, Poland. KTW I, the first building of the project, was completed in 2018 at 66 metres (217 ft). The second tower, KTW II, rises 134 metres (440 ft) and was finished in 2022; it is the tallest building in Katowice and in the Upper Silesia region.

spots.summary: Silesian Museum in Katowice is a museum in the city of Katowice, Poland.

spots.name: Market Square, Katowice

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Market Square in Katowice is a central feature of the Śródmieście district in the city of Katowice, Poland. This market square, the main one in the city, dates to the late 19th century. It has been rebuilt several times, with the latest round of changes currently in progress.

spots.name: Cathedral of Christ the King, Katowice

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Archikatedra Chrystusa Króla w Katowicach is a classicist and modernist archcathedral in Katowice-Śródmieście, Katowice, Poland. Constructed between 1927 and 1955, the Archcathedral of Christ the King is the largest archcathedral and cathedral in Poland, 120,000 metres cubed large.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of Christ the King, Katowice

spots.name: Silesian Park
spots.summary: Silesian Park is a recreation complex in the center of the Metropolis GZM, located in Chorzów in Upper Silesia, Poland. Silesian Park is managed by WPKiW S.A.

spots.name: Silesian Insurgents Memorial
spots.summary: The Silesian Insurgents Memorial in Katowice, southern Poland, it is a monument to those who took part in the three Silesian Uprisings of 1919, 1920 and 1921. These uprisings aimed to make the region of Upper Silesia part of the newly independent Polish state. It is located nearby to the Spodek.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Great Synagogue was a former Jewish congregation and synagogue, located in Katowice, Poland.

spots.name: Parachute Tower in Katowice
spots.summary: Parachute Tower in Katowice is a 35-metre tall lattice parachute tower built in 1937 for training parachute jumps. It was used in the first days of World War II by Germany's 73rd Infantry Division as an observation tower.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: St. Mary's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Mary's Church in Katowice is one of the oldest churches in Katowice, Poland, dating back to 19th century. This neo-Gothic church is located in the Śródmieście district. The architectural design was entrusted to Alexis Langer, a renowned architect from Breslau (Wrocław).

spots.name: Legendia
spots.summary: Legendia is an amusement park located within Silesian Park in the center of the Metropolis GZM, Poland. It has an area of 26 ha. In 2008, the park saw 253,000 visitors.

spots.name: Silesian Zoological Garden
spots.summary: Silesian Zoological Garden is a zoological garden in Poland. It was founded in 1954 and is situated in the Katowice and Chorzów cities in the Metropolis GZM. It covers over 47.6 ha within the Silesian Park.

spots.name: Prezydent Shaft
spots.summary: Prezydent Shaft is a former coal-mine headframe in Chorzów, Silesian Voivodeship, Poland. The reinforced-concrete, single-strut tower is about 42 metres tall and carries two rope sheaves 5.5 metres in diameter.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Kościuszko Park
spots.summary: The Kościuszko Park, which has existed since 1925, is one of the most famous and frequented parks in Katowice, Poland. It is situated at the street of the same name.

spots.name: Silesian Planetarium
spots.summary: The Silesian Planetarium also Silesian Planetarium and Astronomical Observatory is the largest and oldest planetarium in Poland. It was founded on 4 December 1955 to commemorate Nicolaus Copernicus. It is located in the Silesian Park, on the boundary between the Katowice and Chorzów cities in the Metropolis GZM.

spots.name: St. Michael's church, Katowice
spots.summary: Church of St. Michael Archangel is one of the oldest buildings in Katowice. It is located in Kościuszko Park, where it was moved in 1938 from the village Syrynia, where it was originally constructed in 1510. It is under the invocation of St. Michael.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St. Michael the Archangel, Katowice

spots.name: Polish National Radio Symphony Orchestra building
spots.summary: The Headquarters of the Polish National Radio Symphony Orchestra in Katowice is a concert hall located at 1 Wojciech Kilar Square in the Bogucice district of Katowice, Poland.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Headquarters of the Polish National Radio Symphony Orchestra in Katowice

spots.name: Drapacz Chmur
spots.summary: Drapacz Chmur is a historical building in Katowice, Silesia, Poland. It was the second skyscraper built in post-World War I Poland. Finished in 1934 after five years of construction, it made pioneering Polish use of steel frame construction.

spots.name: 3 Maja Street, Katowice
spots.summary: 3 Maja Street in Katowice is a street in the centre ('Śródmieście') of Katowice, Poland. The street was built in the 19th century. During World War II the street was called Grundmannstraße, 1867−1922 Grundmannstraße, 1856−1867 Industriestraße.

spots.name: Katowice Forest Park
spots.summary: Katowice Forest Park is a large park and wooded area in the southern part of the city of Katowice, Poland. It is the largest green area in Katowice, and has been named one of the Upper Silesia area's "most important natural resources".

spots.name: Cathedral of the Resurrection

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Church of the Resurrection in Katowice is a neo-Roman Evangelical-Augsburg church in the Śródmieście district, Katowice, Poland. It was built in the years 1856–1858 and was the first masonry church in Katowice.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Katowice historic railway station
spots.summary: Katowice historic railway station was the main railway station of Katowice, in the Silesia region of what is now Poland. Built in 1859 and reconstructed and expanded several times, it was judged obsolete after World War II, and in 1972 decommissioned and replaced by the newly built Katowice railway station.

spots.name: Młyńska Street
spots.summary: Młyńska Street in Katowice is one of the oldest streets in the Śródmieście district of Katowice. It begins at Market Square, intersects with Wawelska Street, and ends at the junction with Dworcowa Street near Wilhelm Szewczyk Square and the Katowice railway station.

spots.name: Upper Silesian Ethnographic Park
spots.summary: The Upper Silesian Ethnographic Park is an open-air museum in Chorzów, Poland. It is referred to as a skansen, stemming from the first open-air museum of its kind, the Skansen in Stockholm, Sweden. The area of the park is 25 hectares.

spots.name: Stawowa Street
spots.summary: Stawowa Street is one of the most prominent and well-known pedestrian streets in the Śródmieście district of Katowice, Poland. Its name likely derives from a pond that once existed behind Piotr Skarga Street.

spots.summary: St. John Street in Katowice is a street in the Śródmieście district. It begins at the Market Square, intersects with Staromiejska Street and Dworcowa Street, and ends after a railway viaduct at the junction with Tadeusz Kościuszko Street, Jan Kochanowski Street, and Wojewódzka Street.

spots.summary: The Pałac Goldsteinów or Goldstein Palace is neo-Renaissance palace, which was built by two brothers, Abraham and Joseph Goldstein. It is located in Katowice, Silesia, Poland, at the west end of the city centre, at 50°15′33″N 19°0′47″E.

spots.summary: The Kościół św. Szczepana or Saint Stephen's Church is a church in Katowice, Silesian Voivodship, Poland. It is dedicated to Saint Stephen and located at 50°16′9″N 19°2′17″E on Leopold Markiefki street.

spots.name: Silesian Stadium
spots.summary: The Silesian Stadium is a sport stadium located on the premises of Silesian Park in Chorzów, Poland. The stadium has a fully covered capacity of 54,378, after refurbishment completed in October 2017. The stadium hosted many Poland national football team matches and for many decades was Poland's national stadium.

spots.summary: The Scientific Information Center and Academic Library (CINiBA) is a joint scientific library of two universities in Katowice - the University of Silesia in Katowice and the University of Economics in Katowice. It is located in the heart of the university campus, in the center of the Silesian agglomeration.

spots.name: Nikiszowiec
spots.summary: Nikiszowiec is a city neighbourhood built 1908-12 to house workers of Giesche (later Wieczorek) coal mine, all in a distinct red-brick style. It has the neo-Baroque Church of St Mary, several galleries, a branch of the Museum of Katowice History, and a modern hotel.
